title: Structural Problems for $C^*$- and von Neumann Algebras
exact_target: Do the normalized random matrices $X_k$ converge strongly to a free circular distribution? Are $q$-Gaussian $C^*$-algebras selfless for $-1<q<1$ and $q\neq0$? Are the indicated tracial ultrapowers mutually isomorphic? Does there exist a group that has a mixed identity and whose reduced $C^*$-algebra is selfless? Does $C^*(F_2\times F_2)$ have the local lifting property? Does a nonamenable group without free subgroups exist whose reduced $C^*$-algebra has rapid decay? For compact convex $K$, does equality of its minimal and maximal operator-system structures imply that $K$ is a Choquet simplex? Are the free group factors $L(F_2)$ and $L(F_3)$ nonisomorphic? Are the free-product factors $Z(r,\tau)^{*n}$ and $Z(r,\tau)^{*m}$ isomorphic, and is there a dichotomy? Is every unital simple separable $C^*$-algebra singly generated? Do classifiable $C^*$-algebras admit filtrations with rapid decay? Is $F_2$ superrigid among hyperbolic groups at the level of reduced $C^*$-algebras? When is a von Neumann algebra with a faithful state selfless?
